headline: Photosynthesis is the foundation of almost all life—turning sunlight into food
universal_truth: Primary sources matter; everything downstream depends on something upstream
fun_facts: Photosynthesis produces all the oxygen in our atmosphere—every breath you take comes from plants
Plants capture only about 1-2% of the sunlight that hits them, yet this powers nearly all life on Earth
The same process that makes plant food also removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
discussion_questions: Why can't animals make their own food like plants?
How does almost all food trace back to photosynthesis?
What would happen if photosynthesis stopped?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Plants do something miraculous: they eat sunlight. Through photosynthesis, they capture light energy and transform it into sugar—food from nothing but sunshine, water, and air. This simple process powers almost all life on Earth.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Animals eat food. Plants make food. But how? How does a leaf turn light into sugar? What's actually happening during photosynthesis?

options.text: Chlorophyll captures light energy, which powers reactions that combine CO2 and water into sugar
options.response: Yes. Green chlorophyll absorbs sunlight. This energy drives chemical reactions that assemble carbon dioxide and water into glucose—sugar. Light becomes food.

options.text: Plants absorb nutrients from soil and use sunlight to grow
options.response: Soil provides minerals, but the actual food—sugar—is made from air and water, powered by light...

q1.title: Light to Sugar
q1.script: Photosynthesis combines carbon dioxide from air with water from soil, using sunlight as energy. The output: glucose (sugar) and oxygen. Plants literally make food from thin air—carbon atoms from CO2 become the building blocks of all life.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Light to Sugar"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Oxygen Factory
q2.script: The oxygen you're breathing right now came from photosynthesis. Plants split water molecules to get hydrogen, releasing oxygen as a byproduct. Every breath you take connects you to plants—past and present.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Foundation of Life
q3.script: Almost all food chains start with photosynthesis. Plants make sugar; animals eat plants; other animals eat those animals. Even deep-sea ecosystems without light ultimately depend on surface photosynthesis. It's the energy foundation.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Primary sources matter. Photosynthesis teaches that everything downstream depends on something upstream. Understanding the source helps you understand everything that follows.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 143. Tomorrow, we'll discover giants that live for centuries—trees. Until then, thank a plant for the oxygen you're breathing.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Source Tracing - Find the Foundation
growTrack.learning_objective: Trace things back to their primary sources
growTrack.activity: Trace something you use back to its source. Your lunch ultimately came from photosynthesis. Your electricity may come from ancient photosynthesis (fossil fuels) or current photosynthesis (biofuels). What's the primary source powering your day?
